verdict:
NOT READY. Five small record defects need fixing before this can be one commit. The code and most of the records hold up.

What I checked myself in /Users/aldemirkonuk/Projects/wt-finish-train2 (HEAD 22ad1b3a1; 109 files unstaged, +404/-223; no untracked files; no stash from this worktree):

- **B1 holds.** The bracket at PROGRESS.md:110-114 gives ADR 0160's real picks: 110 = B with C kept in mind, 111 = delegated. PROGRESS/STATE contain no other unbracketed restatement, and STATE.md:22 is only a link.

- **B2 code holds, tested both ways.**
  - Before: in a scratch copy of the gateway at HEAD, the new spec against the HEAD digest source failed 1/45 ("Expected number of calls: 1, Received: 0").
  - After: the same copy with the fixed source passed 45/45.
  - In the worktree, src/analytics/digest plus recommendation-digest-pref-read.spec.ts passed 4 suites, 88/88.
  - Gateway tsc passes on both configs (tsconfig.json run with --noEmit). Web tsc passes.
  - No consumer of DIGEST_CATEGORY, categoryOff or preferences.category remains in apps/web or apps/mobile.
  - The five answers (a)-(e) match the memory file word for word.

- **M2 holds on substance.** The heading, Decision, Consequences and "6 of 7" brackets are in. The 8 -> 5 count is right (items 1, 2, 3 and 8 are answered). Commits 82aab7d31 and 9c6387edd are real ancestors of HEAD. The sketch-120 brief is at :160.
  - ADR 0160 also carries a block for Open item 3 ("built 2026-09-19, uncommitted") and a review-trail row signed "Sonnet 5". This round did not write either. They come from a peer session: memory senders-move-to-communications-2026-09-19 says the ADR amendment lives here, the new home is on claude/wizardly-knuth-31d531, and the cut is in wt-pg-promos, all uncommitted. They are fine to carry, but the commit body must say so.

- **M4 holds.**
  - The ADR 0112 F10 bracket and review-trail row quote the founder verbatim.
  - I re-checked Meta's public docs myself:
    - The Messages API reference lists only sending messages, marking them read and the typing indicator. There is nothing for a business to delete, recall or unsend a message it sent.
    - The revoke webhook is only "A WhatsApp user revokes (deletes) a previously sent message".
    - The changelog page returned HTTP 500 to my fetch, so it is unchecked.
  - So only a local-only "delete for me" is buildable, which is what the record says.
  - OD-132 is unique across all 118 worktrees and every ref. The highest id elsewhere is OD-131 in wt-sessions.
  - No existing OD covered the /privacy legal facts (OD-115 is about pooling).

- **M5 holds.**
  - I ran the open row's verify: exit 1 today, as an open row must.
  - A scratch mutant that scopes all 12 methods makes it exit 0, so the row will flip when the gap is fixed.
  - compareProviders and getSentimentTrend do filter by restaurant.
  - The global TenantGuard only sets tenantId and always returns true, so "no tenant check" is accurate.

- **Extended verifies are proven.** On scratch mutants, the old verify passes and the new one catches all three: a raw unsubscribe_token column (old 0 / new 1), md5 instead of sha256 (0/1), and a fixed stop reason (0/1). The previous verifier had not mutated these.

- **Guards, all re-run:**
  - claims: 374/374 holding
  - citation pairing: PASS
  - check_adr_numbers_unique: OK against 934 refs
  - conflict markers: PASS
  - definer self-test: 577 cases OK
  - new-tables self-test: 95 cases OK

- **The 109 files split as follows.** 93 differ only in the digits of OPEN-DECISIONS.md:N citations: 91 by a plain text match, plus LEDGER-FOOD-MIGRATION-OPTIONS.md and foundation/teams/corporate.md, whose citations use link syntax. The other 16 are the substantive edits. The ci.yml change is one example line number (OD-88 is at :56).

Side effects and residue:
- I ran `git fetch -q origin main`. It changes a remote-tracking ref only. origin/main is 2 commits ahead and touches none of the files in this diff.
- apps/api-gateway/dist/ was emitted by the implementer's non-noEmit tsc run. It is gitignored and not committed.

Not blocking, but worth fixing:
- The M2 brackets at ADR 0160 :490-494 and :535-538 say the senders home was "built 2026-09-19" without saying it is uncommitted on other branches. Open item 3 does say so.
- ADR 0160:160-163 says "only the first sentence below is a requirement". The memory says "first part", and the Requirement block is two sentences.

After the fixes, the gate-owned files (ci.yml, decisions/README.md) still need the founder's word before merge (ADR 0090 step 7).

Line 1052 now ends at 'PROGRESS.md:221`' with no closing pipe, its opening `**` never closes inside the cell, and line 1053 renders as a separate, garbled row. Put the row back on ONE line, with the bracket inline. It is the only unterminated table row this diff adds in any .md file (checked: HEAD 0, working tree 1).

.planning/06-pages/recommendations.md, the new '[OPEN, recorded 2026-09-19, PR #391 audit security note 6 ...]' bracket (~:1088-1102) gets the mechanism wrong. It says the digest route has 'no try/catch of its own' and that GET leaks. In fact GET recommendations/:restaurantId/digest (`analytics.controller.ts:1143-1149`) throws a plain Error, which Nest's default BaseExceptionFilter answers with a generic 500 'Internal server error'. The only global interceptor is SentryInterceptor, which rethrows unchanged, and there is no APP_FILTER, so GET does not leak. The real leak is PUT: `analytics.controller.ts:1167-1177` catches and rethrows `error.message` as HttpException(400). That message is setDigestPref's raw `new Error(error.message)` (`recommendation-actions.service.ts:338`) or getDigestPref's interpolated text (`:297-299`). Correct the record in place with a dated bracket: GET is safe, PUT leaks through its controller catch, and the 400 is the wrong status for a database failure.

.planning/06-pages/recommendations.md:1003-1008 -- the 2026-09-17 BUILT paragraph still says the sender 'mails a member only when all five hold: ... and `categories.ai`'. This commit removes that gate, and the line has no bracket. Add a dated bracket saying four facts now; the categories.ai gate was removed 2026-09-19 (PR #391 audit B2(b)), pointing to the ANSWERED bracket below it.

.planning/decisions/README.md:160 -- the ADR 0149 row silently changes 'answers through 2026-09-17' to '2026-09-18' and drops 'nine' from 'nine rounds of answers'. Only the 38 -> 50 change is bracketed, and the rules forbid silent rewrites. Extend the existing bracket to cover both changes, or restore the old words with a bracket.

.planning/06-pages/settings.md -- founder answer (c) (drop the free recipient_email field when #391 lands, and add a per-person 'send me the digest' opt-in on Settings) is recorded only in recommendations.md. The lane that owns the follow-up reads settings.md, which carries no pointer. Add a one-line dated pointer there, naming it a settings-lane follow-up that is not built.

commit_body:
The #391 audit at 22ad1b3a1 blocked on records (B1, B2), listed five medium items (M1-M5) and a set of low notes. The founder answered every open fork on 2026-09-19. This commit writes those answers in and makes the one code change they require.

Code (B2(b), delegated by the founder: "do the most sota, quality, scalability with right architecture structure"):
- The person's recommendation_digest_subscriptions row is now the only consent and the only gate. RecommendationDigestService no longer reads notification_preferences.categories.ai: removed the sweep gate, the statusFor blocker and the preferences.category field; DIGEST_CATEGORY is gone.
- The category-gate spec now asserts that a member with categories.ai:false who is subscribed with email on DOES get the digest.
- Against the pre-fix source it fails 1/45 ("Expected number of calls: 1, Received: 0"); against this source it passes 45/45. The digest suites plus pref-read pass 88/88.

Records:
- B1: PROGRESS.md sketch picks bracketed with ADR 0160's corrections: 110 cellar = B, C kept in mind; 111 help = delegated.
- B2: recommendations.md §9 and §13.7 and ADR 0149 row 26 bracketed with the founder's (a)-(e). (c) (drop the recipient_email field and add a per-person opt-in on Settings) is a follow-up for the settings lane, not built here.
- M1: the production duplicate counts (0 and 0, measured read-only 2026-09-18, re-confirmed 2026-09-19) bracketed at ADR 0121, connections.md and PROGRESS.md.
- M2: ADR 0160 §113's senders/strangers question marked answered (they move to /communications). Open-item count corrected from 8 to 5. Review-trail rows added for 82aab7d31 and 9c6387edd. The sketch-120 feedback recorded as the brief for sketch 122.
- M3: decisions/README.md gains rows for ADR 0160 and ADR 0162. The ADR 0149 row count corrected from 38 to 50.
- M4: locked ADR 0112 F10 amended: a WhatsApp message a person sends by clicking Send needs no seal, in the founder's words. Two follow-ups named, not built: deleting your own messages, and a WhatsApp-Web-like surface in the house frame. Meta's public Cloud API docs have no way for a business to delete a message it sent; the only related feature is the revoke webhook, which reports a user deleting their own message. So only a local "delete for me" is buildable. ADR 0149 row 47 filed as OD-132 (OD-124..131 are allocated to other lanes). check_citation_pairing --fix then repointed 178 citations, which is the only change in 93 of the 109 files.
- M5: new open CLAIMS row TECHDEBT-PROVIDER-INTEL-12-UNSCOPED-READS. Re-reading the source, none of the twelve methods is global by design. A mutant that scopes all twelve flips the verify.
- Notes:
  - The definer check's floor message now tells a hardening PR to lower MIN_PUBLIC_SECDEF with a reason (self-test: 577 cases).
  - ADR 0159 records that production, measured read-only 2026-09-19, has 0 SECURITY DEFINER functions outside extensions that anon or authenticated can execute. It also records that the check never reads production's ACLs.
  - OD-72's stale floors (61/89 -> 576/95) bracketed.
  - The ADR-0149-DIGEST and ADR-0121-F3 verifies extended, and mutation-tested: raw token, md5 and fixed-reason mutants are all caught.
  - ADR 0121's "Land both now" citation corrected (was :139).
  - The digest's database-error-text exposure recorded as an open item.
- Also in this commit: ADR 0160 Open item 3's build record and a review-trail row from a peer session. The senders home is on claude/wizardly-knuth-31d531 and the /promotions cut is in wt-pg-promos, both uncommitted. The founder answered "flip mudavym_design_communications first".

Not built here: the Settings opt-in UI, message delete, the WhatsApp-Web surface, and the fix for the error-text exposure.

Checks: decision claims 374/374; citation pairing PASS; ADR numbers unique (934 refs); no conflict markers; definer self-test 577; new-tables self-test 95; gateway tsc 0 errors on both configs; web tsc 0 errors.
